ABSTRACT: This research introduces the use of deep reinforcement learning (DRL) algorithms to enhance Mobile Edge Computing (MEC) task offloading through 5G networks. The improved DRL task offloading has been designed to minimize energy consumption, to balance the total number of tasks being processed on all edge servers, and to reduce average time required to complete a task via choosing whether to offload tasks to edge servers or execute tasks directly on User Equipments (UE). The task offloading is performed as a Markov Decision Process (MDP) and is accomplished using a Deep Q-Network (DQN). The DQN agent uses information about tasks and the network to make decisions regarding the offloading of tasks. Training stability and learning effectiveness are enhanced through the use of experience replay and a target network in the DQN architecture. When compared with execution of tasks without offloading, task latency is reduced by nearly 60%. In addition, the proposed approach increases CPU utilization on edge servers and yields greater energy savings. Evaluation and implementation of the proposed method has been completed on the Mininet emulator with traffic workloads. Although there are constraints, including dependence, on task profiles and a centralized control agent the experimental findings highlight the approachs scalability and robustness. Overall, the framework offers a practical way to address resource management challenges in evolving edge computing settings, leading to more effective and responsive mobile applications

ABSTRACT: The rapid growth of digital data has exposed significant limitations in traditional clustering methods, particularly with respect to scalability, computational overhead, and clustering quality. To address these challenges, this paper proposes Firefly–K-Means with Tree- and Hash-based optimization (FKTH), a scalable distributed clustering framework that integrates an adaptive Firefly Algorithm (FA) with K-Means, enhanced through KD-Tree–based distance computation, hash map–based constant-time centroid updates, and Hadoop MapReduce–based parallel processing. The adaptive Firefly component dynamically adjusts attraction, absorption, and randomness parameters during optimization to balance exploration and exploitation and avoid premature convergence. The proposed framework is evaluated on large-scale real-world datasets ranging from 100K to over 1M records across varying cluster node configurations. Experimental results demonstrate that FKTH achieves superior scalability and consistently outperforms existing metaheuristic-based clustering methods in terms of execution time, Silhouette Score, Davies–Bouldin Index (DBI), and F1-score, making it well suited for large-scale distributed data analytics.

ABSTRACT: Action recognition in videos plays an important role in areas like surveillance, sports analytics, and other intelligent systems. Models that rely only on visual input often run into problems, especially when parts of the scene are blocked or when two actions look very similar. In this work, we look at how combining audio and visual cues may help with these limitations. Three of the implementations are based on these four classes from the UCF101 dataset—BoxingPunchingBag, Archery, PlayingCello, and PlayingDaf to keep the setup manageable. While one implementation uses a different set: PlayingSitar, PlayingFlute, SkyDiving, Typing, and TableTennisShot. Visual features are taken from pretrained backbones such as ResNet50, ViT, EfficientNetB0, and MobileNetV3Small. The audio features come from log-mel spectrograms and Wav2Vec2 embeddings. We tested two fusion approaches: simple concatenation and Gated Fusion across several classifiers, including a Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN), a Multilayer Perceptron (MLP), a Vision Transformer with audio, and a Bidirectional LSTM (Bi-LSTM). Among all the models, the Bi-LSTM with Gated Fusion achieves the highest accuracy at 99%. The ViT-based multimodal model follows at 98%, and the MLP and TCN reach 70.08% and 57%. These results suggest that incorporating temporal information and using an adaptive fusion method appears to make a noticeable difference in action recognition. ABSTRACT: In this paper, we propose a benchmark dataset for categorization of fabric into two tasks: i) Classification of a given material into Silk versus Non-silk. ii) Identification of viewing method-Handloom or Powerloom. Hence, there is an absence of an RGB dataset that captures fabric weave geometry and contains samples from broader categories that jointly addresses two major tasks of textiles. The fabrics used are colourless and without prints to ensure that the dataset consists of images which are focused on the warp-weft structure of the fabric, and while training, the models are not affected by colour, patterns, prints or motifs during evaluation. ABSTRACT: MRI scans tend to struggle with low spatial resolution. Hardware limits, long scan times, and patient movement all play a part. ABSTRACT: Medical question answering systems increasingly rely on large language models for fluent responses, but their use in healthcare is constrained by hallucinations, limited domain control, and lack of verified evidence. Retrieval augmented generation improves factual grounding using external sources, yet many traditional RAG pipelines process queries independently and offer limited support for multi turn interactions, conversational context preservation, and answer reuse. This paper presents MedNexus, a decision centric medical question answering system designed as a reliable assistive tool rather than a generative authority. MedNexus follows a structured execution pipeline consisting of Follow Up Reasoning to resolve context dependent queries, Cache Augmented Generation to reuse previously validated answers, Retrieval Augmented Generation with cross encoder reranking over trusted biomedical sources, and Agentic Context Enhancement for adaptive response presentation. Generative models are invoked only when retrieval confidence is insufficient. Experimental evaluation on curated biomedical queries demonstrates high domain scope detection accuracy, strong hallucination avoidance, reliable follow up resolution in multi turn interactions, and reduced response latency over repeated use. These results highlight the importance of controlled RAG pipelines that combine evidence grounding with conversational robustness for safe and practical medical question answering

ABSTRACT: Over the past few years, deep learning has completely changed the way we think about AI, with advances in all the domains. Quantization is a key optimization technique which reduces the model size and computational requirements but even it faces issues because of the presence of the outliers in weight distribution causing performance degradation. ABSTRACT: 5G technology advancements are transforming the manner in which vehicles communicate to make transportation safer, more efficient, and more effectively managed. Cellular Vehicle-to-Everything (C-V2X) technology, specifically 5G New Radio (NR), complements vehicle sensing capabilities by allowing direct and network-assisted communication to enhance situational awareness—even under non-line-of-sight circumstances. This research examines the performance of 5G NR-V2X under vehicle platooning conditions to examine latency, throughput, and resource allocation under different vehicle speeds and inter-vehicle distances. A simulation of the MAC layer was created to assess sidelink resource allocation with semi-persistent scheduling considering vehicles with varying speeds broadcasting periodic safety messages. Performance parameters were examined at different speeds (20–30 mph) and distances (50–200 m). Results demonstrate that low speeds and low distances enhance latency and throughput through improved sync and resource allocation, but increased speeds and wider spacing make the system less communicatively efficient. ABSTRACT: Adverse Drug Reactions (ADRs), which often emerge in post-market surveillance or late-stage clinical trials, remain one of the biggest challenges in pharmaceutical safety. Challenges with existing computational models for ADR prediction involve inadequate protein-level representation and limited biological interpretability. Focusing on finding the optimal models, this research provides a comprehensive evaluation of different modeling strategies—deep learning, machine learning, and statistical methods for ADR pre- diction. We enhance protein-drug interaction (PDI) modeling by generating biologically interpretable protein embeddings through ProGen, a generative protein sequence model. A variety of deep learning models (Feed-Forward Neural Networks, Convolu- tional Neural Networks, Token Transformers, Graph Neural Networks), in addition to baseline machine learning (Random Forests, Support Vector Machines) and statistical approaches (Logistic Regression), utilize these embeddings along with drug molecular descriptors.Since ADR datasets in the real world are limited, experiments were conducted on a synthetic 1,000 drug-protein combi- nation dataset. ABSTRACT: As 5G networks evolve toward open and disaggregated architectures, intelligent RAN control becomes essential for maintaining service quality under diverse mobility scenarios. This paper presents a simulation-driven framework for intelligent handover decision-making using KPM (Key Performance Measurement) data collected via an O-RAN-compliant xApp. The proposed system monitors UE-level and cell-level metrics such as RSRP, SINR, PRB usage, and throughput to identify suboptimal radio conditions. A machine learning model (Random Forest) is trained offline on this data to learn patterns associated with successful handovers. While the current implementation does not integrate the trained model into the xApp, the simulation results demonstrate the model’s potential to enable proactive, quality-aware mobility decisions. This work lays the foundation for future integration of learning-based decision logic into real-time RIC xApps

SOURCE PUBLICATION: Procedia Computer Science

ABSTRACT: Blockchain networks rely on consensus mechanisms to maintain security and efficiency. Delegated Proof of Stake (DPoS) is a widely adopted alternative to traditional Proof of Work (PoW) and Proof of Stake (PoS) due to its scalability. However, DPoS suffers from centralization risks, collusion, and the presence of unreliable validators, compromising network integrity. One approach to mitigating these issues is the downgrade method, which reduces the influence of dishonest validators over time by penalizing their stake or voting power. While this approach improves security, it still faces challenges related to manipulation and inefficiency. To address these limitations more effectively, we introduce Game Theory-based Delegated Proof of Stake (GT-DPoS), an advanced consensus framework that integrates strategic decision-making through game theory to optimize node selection and incentivization. GT-DPoS utilizes a two-stage evaluation mechanism based on Reputation Score (RS) and Trust Score (TS) to regulate node behavior, penalize malicious actors, and reward honest participation. In Stage 1, nodes are assessed based on RS, incorporating factors like stake, transaction efficiency, block contribution, and past misconduct. Nodes failing to meet the threshold are penalized, while eligible ones advance to second stage. Stage 2 evaluates TS, considering rewards, penalties, and community votes, refining the selection through a payoff-based model that ensures rational decision-making. Unlike the downgrade method, GT-DPoS provides a more dynamic and adaptive approach, ensuring continuous security enhancement without long-term inefficiencies. Experimental results demonstrate that GT-DPoS achieves faster block creation times compared to conventional DPoS, with up to 4.6% improvement at lower transaction loads and 1.2% at higher loads. By leveraging game-theoretic principles, GT-DPoS enhances decentralization, reduces transaction latency, and strengthens network security, making it a more effective and performance-optimized alternative to both traditional DPoS and downgrade-based approaches

ABSTRACT: Fifth-generation (5G) networks are designed to support a vast array of services like enriched mobile broadband (eMBB), ultra-reliable low-latency communication (URLLC), and massive machine-type communication (mMTC), each needing special Quality of Service (QoS) assurance. To address these varied needs, network slicing supports the formation of virtualized and segregated network slices. But ensuring real-time optimization of slices is still a challenging task. This paper presents an intelligent 5G network slicing framework which integrates Open5GS and UERANSIM to simulate the core and radio access network, machine learning methods for anomaly detection, and reinforcement learning to adaptively tune performance. In particular, a Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) agent is learned in a special environment to make slice-level decisions using real-time latency and throughput measurements. Experimental results show that the eMBB slice achieved its throughput from 550 Mbps to 900 Mbps and reduced latency from 35 ms to 15 ms. The URLLC slice had persistent low latency at 2 ms, while mMTC exhibited a remarkable reduction in packet loss from 0.6% to 0.1%. Under mixed traffic loads scenario, the framework managed to balance resources among slices without domination by a single service type and maintaining compliance with QoS restrictions. These results demonstrate the future potential of the presented AI-based framework in providing adaptive, efficient, and SLA-conformant network slicing for future wireless networks.

PUBLICATION TITLE: Load Balancing in 5G Networks: A Virtual-Radius Based Approach
SOURCE PUBLICATION: Procedia Computer Science
AUTHOR ADDRESS: Ashwini R Jannu, KLE Technological University, Hubballi, India, School of Computer Science and Engineering, Computer Science and Engineering|Jayalaxmi Naragund G [232736], KLE Technological University, Hubballi, India, School of Computer Science and Engineering, Computer Science and Engineering
ABSTRACT: Efficient load balancing is essential in 5G heterogeneous networks because an imbalance in the distribution of traffic between macro and small cells produces congestion, reduced throughput, excessive handovers, and unfair allocation of radio resources. These challenges become more severe in dense urban environments where variable traffic, user mobility, and random placement of small cells results in significant network load variations. To address this issue, the proposed virtual-radius based load balancing algorithm dynamically adjusts each cell’s effective coverage based on real-time network conditions. It continuously assesses parameters such as cell utilization, user density, interference levels, mobility speeds, and QoS requirements and then adaptively expands or shrinks the virtual radius of each cell to offload or attract users. Predictive load estimation thus facilitates proactive traffic steering before congestion actually builds up. The performance of the proposed algorithm was evaluated with a hybrid dataset: real locations of macro towers combined with synthetically generated small-cell deployments. Large-scale simulations were performed with 1,200 mobile users distributed over 10 macro cells, each having 3 to 5 small cells. Various parameters impact performance, like traffic types, interference variations, and handover thresholds. Simulation results show a 38% increase in total throughput along with a 20.5% decrease in congestion within macro cells and a 50% increase in small-cell utilization. A 26.7% reduction in the handover rate, along with an increase in Jain’s fairness index from 0.72 to 0.89, is also achieved, showing a better balance in radio resource distribution. The algorithm demonstrates polynomial-time complexity: it is linear for user-position updates, linear for load monitoring, and quadratic for radius adjustments with interference awareness. The efficiency certifes that the proposed method is feasible for real-time 5G deployment.

ABSTRACT: The Tactile Internet (TI) compels hard demands on ultra-low latency and high reliability, which makes the management of the caches a tremendous challenge in the context of multi-slice Mobile Edge Computing (MEC). Current caching solutions are mostly slice-blind, and do not support a combination of the heterogeneous Quality-of-Service (QoS) requirements of Ultra-Reliable Low-Latency Communications (URLLC), enhanced Mobile Broadband (eMBB), and machine-type communications of massive scale, mMTC. In the present paper, a Slice-Weighted Scoring Cache (SWSC) framework to content admission and eviction has been proposed, incorporating slice urgency, content popularity, and time to live (TTL) decay as a single utility. The cache management issue is defined as a maximization of utility task, and thus, efficient greedy solution can be obtained in the capacity-constrained setting. The algorithm suggested utilizes a heap-based dynamic prioritization and eviction mechanism of content. Massive simulations show that SWSC is far more effective in improving cache hit rates, performance, reducing cache miss rates, and improving aggregate cache efficiency relative to the baseline algorithms, including LRU, LRU-TTL and Q-learning-based caching. The findings confirm that SWSC is useful in addressing next-generation applications that are latency-sensitive

AUTHOR ADDRESS: Humakousar Sangreskop, University of Agricultural Sciences, Bangalore, India, Applied Mathematics and Computer Science, Agricultural Statistics|Uma Mudengudi [232799], KLE Technological University, Hubballi, India, School of Electrical and Electronics Engineering, Electronics and Communication Engineering|Sujatha C [232737], KLE Technological University, Hubballi, India, School of Computer Science and Engineering, Computer Science and Engineering
ABSTRACT: In this paper, we propose a framework for classifying mulberry silk fabric as either handloom or powerloom using RGB images. Distinguishing between these weaving methods is challenging because both weaving methods generate textiles with highly similar visual appearance, texture, and color characteristics. The challenge becomes more pronounced when fabrics originate from the same material category. Existing approaches rely primarily on visual texture and appearance cues while overlooking the intrinsic structural characteristics introduced by the weaving process. However, the distinguishing features of handloom and powerloom fabrics often lie in repetitive structural patterns, including weave regularity, orientation, and periodic arrangements are used by most models, thereby degrading performance in fine-grained fabric analysis. To address this, we propose FEViT, a dual-branch transformer-based model where one branch learns visual features from RGB images, while the other captures structural information using Discrete Cosine Transform (DCT), which helps represent repeating patterns and frequency details in the fabric. Both branches use Swin Transformer backbones, and their features are combined to make the final prediction. Along with this, we perform detailed structural analysis using edge, orientation, and frequency-based features, and validate the findings across different fabrics such as cotton, milk fibre, orange fibre, soya, and hemp. Statistical evaluation confirms significant structural differences between handloom and powerloom fabrics (p < 0.05). Edge-density and orientation-based descriptors exhibit strong discriminative capability, while frequency-domain representations provide complementary structural information that motivates the frequency-enhanced design of the proposed framework. Although DCT entropy alone shows a relatively small effect size (|d| = 0.29), frequency-domain features capture structural periodicities and weave regularities that are not readily observable in the spatial domain. Experimental results demonstrate that FEViT achieves an accuracy of 98.11%, outperforming conventional appearance-based models and highlighting the effectiveness of jointly learning spatial and frequency-domain fabric representations for loom classification

ABSTRACT: Edge-cloud computing enables low-latency service delivery by deploying applications closer to end users. However, dynamic and bursty workloads pose significant challenges to efficient resource management. Traditional Kubernetes Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (HPA) relies on reactive scaling mechanisms, which often result in delayed responses, resource inefficiencies, and degraded Quality of Service (QoS). This work presents a predictive autoscaling and scheduling framework based on Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) for Kubernetes-enabled edge-cloud environments using KubeEdge. The framework leverages LSTM networks to estimate future CPU and memory usage at both pod and node levels, thereby facilitating proactive scaling decisions. Additionally, an intelligent scheduling mechanism utilises predicted resource availability to optimise pod placement across heterogeneous edge nodes. Experimental evaluation under dynamic workloads demonstrates that the proposed framework reduces response time by 18−25% and improves throughput by 15−22% compared to the default HPA and standalone LSTM autoscaling. The results confirm that integrating predictive autoscaling with scheduling enhances scalability, responsiveness, and resource utilisation in edge-cloud deployments

ABSTRACT: The 5G technology offers capabilities such as ultralow latency, high data rates, and reliable communication. However, extensive dependency on centralized cloud computing causes additional end-to-end delays and congestion. To address this issue, this study proposes implementing an intelligent mechanism for offloading tasks, considering 5G-enabled edge computing and cloud computing. AUTHOR ADDRESS: Prajwal Ganeshanavar, KLE Technological University, Hubballi, India, School of Computer Science and Engineering, Computer Science and Engineering|Narayan D G [232716], KLE Technological University, Hubballi, India, School of Computer Science and Engineering, Computer Science and Engineering|Sadaf Savanur, KLE Technological University, Hubballi, India, School of Computer Science and Engineering, Computer Science and Engineering|Amit Kachavimath [232619], KLE Technological University, Hubballi, India, School of Computer Science and Engineering, Computer Application|Hiremath P S [232613], KLE Technological University, Hubballi, India, School of Computer Science and Engineering, Computer Application
ABSTRACT: The placement of Service Function Chains (SFCs) in edge computing settings becomes increasingly difficult especially when workloads change constantly and hardware resources are limited, more so when applications need minimum latency. Most of the existing SFC placement approaches heavily depend on reactive scheduling or static rules, which are not always effective in such highly dynamic situations. We have developed a framework for adaptive SFC placement that combines decision, based scheduling with workload prediction for a cloud, edge Kubernetes setup. Based on the CPU, memory, and round, trip time (RTT) data collected in the past from the cluster, an LSTM model identifies temporal patterns. Using sliding windows of previous measurements, the worker nodes are categorized as lightly loaded, moderately loaded, and heavily loaded. The model's classification accuracy on the testbed dataset is 96.34%; on the Alibaba Cluster Trace dataset, it is 92.22%. By not relying solely on the present states of the system, these forecasts enable the scheduler to make placement decisions based on expected future states. An auction, based heuristic method is applied to select a suitable node while encouraging stability and fairness among the nodes when they happen to belong to the same load category. The suggested technique is tested under several traffic scenarios and compared with an LSTM only approach and the default Kubernetes scheduler. Experimental results show that the hybrid LSTM and auction, based method can increase throughput by around 22-25% and at the same time have a lower average latency. In general, these results suggest that the issue of SFC placement in dynamic edge computing environments can be more effectively addressed by integrating predictive modeling with fairness, aware decision making

ABSTRACT: Traditional Proof of Work (PoW) consensus protocols in blockchain networks have been criticized for being highly energy-intensive, less scalable, and prone to fairness issues that favor the computations of more powerful miners. To address the aforementioned challenges, we have proposed the development of the Game-Theoretic Proof of Useful Work (GT-PoUW) consensus protocol, which combines the concepts of Federated Learning (FL) with dynamic incentive-revision systems. In this proposed system, every node maintains the capability to train an individual machine learning model, while the selection process for the miners would be based on the accuracy across different models, rather than hash power. This would enable the utilization of the computational power for productive work. To this end, a gametheoretical approach is used for controlling miner classification, update performance, and the dynamic downgrade process in order to effectively prevent malicious miners and encourage honest ones. Experiments reveal that GT-PoUW effectively promotes fairness, which improves Jain's Fairness Index values from 0.7196 in the case of PoW to 0.9537 in the case of PoUW, besides eliminating miner centralization by making the block delivery irrelevant to hashing power. ABSTRACT: Proof-of-Work (PoW)-based consensus mechanisms have been shown to be vulnerable to strategic mining attacks such as selfish mining and block withholding, where rational miners deviate from honest behavior to maximize their rewards. A fundamental challenge associated with these attacks is that many existing solutions are either purely theoretical and difficult to deploy in real-world networks or rely on computationally intensive machine learning techniques. Such approaches often introduce high latency, typically proportional to the number of participating nodes, and are trained on limited attack datasets. To address these limitations, this work introduces a lightweight statistical anomaly detection framework designed to integrate directly with the Ethereum consensus layer. The framework defines a multi-factor risk score, denoted as Rf or k, to evaluate the likelihood and impact of fork-related risks. This score incorporates several key signals, including entropy of block arrival times, chain growth rate, chain depth, and miner diversity. In addition, miner behavior is analyzed through a realtime Miner Score (M-Score), computed using Kullback-Leibler divergence with respect to a trusted reference miner, thereby capturing deviations from expected mining patterns. Experimental evaluation conducted on a private Ethereum test network and within the BlockSim simulation environment demonstrates that the proposed approach achieves a detection accuracy of 95.67% for selfish mining attacks

ABSTRACT: Byzantine Fault Tolerance (BFT) consensus mechanisms are vital for ensuring reliability in permissioned blockchain networks. However, existing BFT implementations such as Quorum-based BFT (QBFT), Istanbul BFT (IBFT) 2.0, and CLIQUE within the Hyperledger Besu framework face significant challenges, including high resource consumption, limited throughput, and scalability bottlenecks, particularly under complex and high-volume smart contract workloads. In this paper, we propose Dynamic Adaptive Byzantine Fault Tolerance (DABFT), a novel consensus framework designed to address these limitations through Adaptive Quorum Selection (AQS) and Optimized Transaction Batching (OTB). We evaluate DABFT using Hyperledger Caliper, benchmarking its performance against established BFT protocols under diverse transaction loads and operational conditions. The results demonstrate that DABFT achieves up to 30% higher throughput, 25% lower latency, and a 15% reduction in resource usage compared to QBFT. These improvements highlight DABFT’s potential to significantly enhance the performance, scalability, and resource efficiency of enterprise-grade blockchain deployments.

Modern methods in the form of inpainting-based GANs, hyperbolic embedding-based generative networks, and GFP-GAN, Generative Facial Prior GAN, rely on semantic understanding coupled with generative modeling to make high-quality results. framework combines the spatial feature extraction capabilities of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs)
with the temporal sequence analysis strengths of Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), effectively integrating

ABSTRACT: Software-defined networking (SDN) is now widely used in modern network infrastructures, but its centralized control design makes it vulnerable to distributed denial of service (DDoS) attacks targeting the SDN controller. These attacks are capable of disrupting the operation of the network and reducing its availability for genuine users. Existing detection and mitigation methods often suffer from numerous drawbacks, such as high computational costs and frequent false alarms, especially with standard machine learning or basic unsupervised approaches. To address these issues, a new framework is proposed that relies on multistep feature selection methods, including SelectKBest, ANOVA-F, and random forest to select the most important network features, to detect anomalies in an unsupervised manner using agglomerative clustering in order identify suspicious hosts, and to mitigate adverse impacts by relying on posterior probability and game theory. An evaluation conducted using benchmark datasets and validated through Mininet emulation demonstrates that the approach achieves better performance with silhouette scores of 0.86 for InSDN and 0.95 for Mininet. The framework efficiently computes reputation scores to distinguish malicious hosts, thus enabling to rely on adaptive defense against evolving attack patterns while maintaining minimal computational overhead.

ABSTRACT: In this paper, we propose a novel framework, Disentangled Style-Content GAN (DISC-GAN), which integrates style-content disentanglement with a cluster-specific training strategy towards photorealistic underwater image synthesis. The quality of synthetic underwater images is challenged by optical due to phenomena such as color attenuation and turbidity. These phenomena are represented by distinct stylistic variations across different waterbodies, such as changes in tint and haze. While generative models are well-suited to capture complex patterns, they often lack the ability to model the non-uniform conditions of diverse underwater environments. To address these challenges, we employ K-means clustering to partition a dataset into style-specific domains. We use separate encoders to get latent spaces for style and content; we further integrate these latent representations via Adaptive Instance Normalization (AdaIN) and decode the result to produce the final synthetic image. The model is trained independently on each style cluster to preserve domain-specific characteristics. Our framework demonstrates state-of-the-art performance, obtaining a Structural Similarity Index (SSIM) of 0.9012, an average Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) of 32.5118 dB, and a Frechet Inception Distance (FID) of 13.3728.

ABSTRACT: Blockchain technology has revolutionized decentralized systems, with applications that span finance, healthcare, and supply chain management. ABSTRACT: Brain tumor segmentation is a critical task in medical imaging, aiding in diagnosis and treatment planning for brain tumor patients. This study presents an enhanced 3D U-Net architecture integrated with Feature Pyramid Networks (FPNs) and attention mechanisms to improve segmentation accuracy. Utilizing the BraTS 2020 dataset, which comprises multimodal MRI scans (T1, T2, T1ce, and FLAIR sequences), the data preprocessing involved intensity normalization, alignment of segmentation masks, and organization of 3D MRI scans. The architecture incorporates an encoder, bottleneck, and decoder path, leveraging FPN for multi-resolution feature extraction and attention mechanisms for tumor region focus. A combination of categorical cross-entropy and Dice loss optimized with the Adam optimizer was employed during training. The model achieved a training accuracy of 96.16%, Dice loss of 0.0086, a test accuracy of 96.14%, and F1-score of 98.03%, outperforming other baselines, including U-Net and its variants. Practical applications include automating tumor segmentation to assist in diagnosis, surgical planning, and treatment monitoring, improving radiological workflows’ speed and precision. However, challenges such as high computational demands and limited dataset diversity remain, requiring further optimization for resource-constrained environments and validation on larger, multi-institutional datasets. This study highlights the potential of combining FPN and attention mechanisms to advance clinical tumor segmentation workflows, with scope for scalability and integration into real-world medical imaging systems

ABSTRACT: Retinal image segmentation with deep learning models has a great deal of promise to increase ophthalmology diagnostic precision. But these models’ intrinsic complexity frequently makes it difficult to understand and interpret the segmentation results. In past research, there have been various methods proposed for segmentation. However, the challenges still exist using the deep learning methods in medical healthcare. In this study, a novel method to improve the transparency and interpretability of retinal image segmentation is proposed by combining the EfficientNet and Explainable AI (XAI) methodologies with the U-Net architecture. Through the use of Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations (LIME), our methodology produces feature visualizations that clarify the U-Net model’s decision-making process, enabling doctors to confirm and understand the segmentation outcomes. The performance metrics measured are Precision, Recall, and F1-score. The precision obtained by means of LIME is 80%. By bridging the gap between high-performance segmentation models and their useful applications in clinical settings, to improve model generalizability across various datasets, the study uses sophisticated data augmentation techniques such as noise addition, brightness fluctuations, and random rotation. The study also points out drawbacks, such as processing overhead and the effect of dataset diversity and size on model performance, paving the potential for further improvements. This integration of XAI approach seeks to encourage trust and enable more informed medical decisions.

ABSTRACT: Monitoring fetal health is crucial to early detection of developmental risks and pregnancy complications. The generator has been modified to include residual blocks to improve features learning and the discriminator is informed by structural edge information to improve the accuracy of the vessel boundary. ABSTRACT: Grasping the dynamics of blood flow is essential for exploring cardiovascular health and identifying irregularities. The insights gained from the initial model inform the development of a three-dimensional (3D) microfluidic model, enhanced with slice simulations to accurately represent velocity fields and pressure gradients. A crucial element of the research involves developing a microfluidic device that mimics the physical and material properties of real arterial systems. The model features layers that resemble the characteristics of media and adventitia, essential for mimicking the mechanical traits of arterial walls. The final simulation includes a lifelike arterial wall constructed from myocardium material, enabling thorough analysis of velocity profiles and pressure distributions. ABSTRACT: Paraphrasing in the context of low-resource languages suffers from scarcity of large paraphrase corpus, which impacts several downstream tasks where paraphrasing is essential. ABSTRACT: This study analyses the thyroid disease dataset obtained from Kaggle, originally sourced from Garavan Institute in Sydney, Australia, which consists of 3771 cases, to uncover patterns and understand the consequences of this non-communicable disease. The study carried out a thorough analysis of the prevalence of hypothyroidism across age and gender brackets and built a model that would predict the presence of hypothyroidism. The data is cleaned by removing sparse attributes, addressing outliers using the Winsorization method, and handling missing values using techniques like central tendencies. Biasness was removed using Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique, and Age was converted to categories using Data Discretization for easy analysis. It is found that the prevalence of hypothyroidism is higher in females (63.24%) when compared to males (28.44%). And adult women (ages 20–59) had the highest positive test rate (54.70%), followed by elderly women (ages 60–100) at (40.98%). Hormonal imbalances, majorly involving T3 (Triiodothyronine), TT4 (Total Thyroxine), and TSH (Thyroid-stimulating hormone), were predominant factors in hypothyroidism. Elevated TSH and normal T3 and T4U (Thyroxine Uptake) indicated subclinical hypothyroidism, especially in adult and elderly women (79%). Screening is recommended for anyone with abnormal hormone levels, as there is an 82.79% chance of having moderate or secondary hypothyroidism. A hypothyroidism predictive model was built using various classification algorithms, among which the Gradient Booster model performed well with an accuracy of 96.37%. The study highlights the need for early detection, particularly considering the significant impact of gender and age on hypothyroidism prevalence, suggesting targeted healthcare interventions

ABSTRACT: Accurately capturing unsteady flow phenomena and complex fluid dynamics is essential for understanding and predicting arterial blood flow behavior. This study leverages computational fluid dynamics (CFD) and machine learning (ML) to detect regions of elevated shear stress in the aorta, focusing on the dynamic responses of arteries under varying hemodynamic conditions. The geometric model of the human aorta was sourced from the Vascular Database, which is supported by SimVascular and includes all necessary boundary conditions. Simulations were performed using the Navier-Stokes equations within SimVascular to generate vtk files containing velocity and pressure data. Since these files could not be directly used for ML training, additional post-processing was conducted in ParaView. By applying specific functions, we extracted key metrics such as pressure, velocity, wall shear stress, and other parameters at multiple spatial coordinates. This resulted in a CSV dataset comprising 23,777 points with corresponding attributes for further analysis of high wall shear stress regions. A Random Forest classifier was trained on this dataset to predict regions of high wall shear stress of the aorta by analyzing attributes like pressure, velocity, and wall shear stress, providing precise coordinate-based predictions of areas with abnormal hemodynamic stress. In our analysis, regions of elevated shear stress were detected at 1,288 points, representing 5.42% of the total dataset. By integrating CFD with ML, we successfully identified regions of high wall shear stress in the aorta, enhancing clinical diagnostic accuracy and offering a data-driven alternative to traditional cardiovascular diagnostic techniques. This study underscores the value of combining CFD and ML to reduce reliance on traditional cardiovascular tests, streamlining diagnosis and therapeutic planning while reducing costs and complexity

ABSTRACT: Cardiac arrhythmias pose a significant challenge in clinical diagnostics, necessitating accurate and efficient detection methods. This study explores the classification of arrhythmias using advanced machine learning models, including Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, and Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs). A dataset of 16,000 simulated ECG signals, generated using SimVascular, provided the foundation for training and evaluation. CNNs achieved high accuracy in spatial feature extraction, while LSTMs excelled in capturing temporal dependencies in sequential ECG data. PINNs emerged as the most robust model, achieving a training accuracy of 97.8% and a testing accuracy of 97.2%, leveraging domain-specific constraints from the FitzHugh-Nagumo equations. The results highlight the complementary strengths of these models, with PINNs offering superior interpretability and physiological consistency. Future work will focus on integrating multi-modal data and developing real-time systems to advance arrhythmia diagnostics and improve cardiac care outcomes

ABSTRACT: Accurate stock price movement prediction remains a intricate problem due to the non-linear and volatile nature of financial markets. Traditional statistical methods and machine learning approaches often struggle to capture long-term temporal dependencies and the dynamic behavior of stock trends. Recent advances in deep learning, particularly Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) models, offer improved capabilities for time-series modeling. This study investigates stock price movement predictions specifically the likelihood of a stock's gain or fall using historical stock data from 2020 to 2024. Four deep learning configurations were analyzed: univariate and multivariate RNNs, and univariate and multivariate LSTMs. Models were trained using 10-fold cross-validation and a batch size of 32. Experimental findings reveal that both univariate and multivariate LSTM models consistently outperform their RNN counterparts, highlighting LSTM’s superior ability to learn from sequential patterns. However, multivariate configurations did not yield significant gains over univariate models, likely due to limited inter-feature correlations and data sparsity. Our findings underscore the effectiveness of deep learning particularly LSTMs in financial forecasting while identifying limitations in multivariate architectures. This study provides a foundation for future work in refining multivariate strategies and benchmarking with hybrid or ensemble models for enhanced stock market prediction.

ABSTRACT: The study proposes a novel semi-supervised deep learning framework called Residual Cross-Fusion Network (ResCrossNet) for hyperspectral deforestation change detection. The model processes a pair of hyperspectral images captured at different time intervals over the same geographical area, using identical spatial-spectral feature extraction pipelines. The Spatial-Spectral Feature Extraction Module (SSFM) incorporates residual spatial and residual channel attention blocks to effectively capture meaningful spatial and spectral information. These extracted features are then subjected to the Cross-Fuse Module (CFM), which increases complementary features and reduces redundancy between the bi-temporal inputs. The fused features are integrated using differencing and concatenation techniques to detect both obvious and subtle changes in the forest landscape. Finally, semantic segmentation is performed using the Refined Object-Contextual Representation (ROCR) module, which models object-level contextual dependencies to increase the accuracy of pixel-level change. Its excellent categorization accuracy of 99.6% when implemented with Python showed its potential for accurate and scalable monitoring of forest change.

ABSTRACT: The focus of this study is to analyze and visualize the patterns of infant mortality across different districts in Karnataka from 2017-2020, with a goal of understanding the key factors causing it. The infant mortality rate has steadily declined, from 13 deaths per 1,000 live births in 2017–18 to 11 in 2019–20. However, certain districts show higher death rates compared to others, indicating the need for targeted healthcare improvements. The analysis reveals that nearly 45% of infant deaths were caused by Asphyxia, followed by 30% from Sepsis and 18% from Pneumonia. In addition, disparities in vaccination distribution and access to health services were evident in areas with higher mortality. By highlighting these patterns and disparities, this study suggests policymakers and healthcare providers to focus their efforts on high-risk regions and causes. The study also explores the factors that improves the infant survival such as strengthening healthcare infrastructure, improving maternal awareness, and ensuring timely vaccinations. Karnataka has made notable progress in reducing infant mortality, but focused interventions in underdeveloped districts are essential to continue this positive trend and ensure every child has a healthy start to life.

ABSTRACT: This study aims to support early diagnosis and treatment planning for dementia using a merged dataset combining clinical and cognitive data from multiple sources [1], [2]. ABSTRACT: This paper presents a comprehensive performance evaluation of a novel TCP variant, TCP ENewReno, designed to enhance congestion control efficiency in high-density and delay-sensitive network environments. TCP ENewReno introduces an adaptive congestion avoidance mechanism that leverages real-time bandwidth estimation through acknowledgment (ACK) intervals to dynamically adjust the congestion window size (CWND). Using NS-2 simulations, we compared TCP ENewReno against traditional TCP Reno and TCP NewReno variants across four critical metrics: Throughput, End-to-End Delay, Congestion Window Size, and Jain’s Fairness Index (JFI). The simulations were conducted over a high-density, mixed wired-wireless topology involving 300 User Equipment (UE) nodes, each initiating FTP sessions under uniform load conditions. Results show that TCP ENewReno consistently outperforms its counterparts, achieving up to 34% higher throughput, more stable and lower delay, better congestion window utilization, and the highest fairness index. These findings highlight TCP ENewReno’s capability to maintain efficient and fair resource utilization under dynamic network conditions, making it a promising solution for emerging 5G and next-generation networking scenarios.

ABSTRACT: The growing demand for differentiated services in 5G networks has led to the adoption of network slicing to support heterogeneous use cases such as enhanced Mobile Broadband (eMBB) and massive Machine-Type Communications (mMTC). Traditional RAN architectures fall short in delivering isolated and service-specific performance. In this work, we present a proof-of-concept ORAN-aligned 5G slicing testbed built entirely using open-source components. The system integrates Open5GS as the 5G Core and UERANSIM for emulating gNB and UE behavior. Two static slices—eMBB and mMTC—are configured using distinct DNNs and dedicated UPF instances to enforce service-level isolation. Performance validation is conducted using iperf3-driven TCP and UDP traffic for the eMBB slice, achieving stable throughput over 50 Mbps in both uplink and downlink. The mMTC slice is simulated using synthetic telemetry-style traffic to reflect low-data-rate IoT scenarios. Prometheus and Grafana are integrated for end-to-end observability, enabling slice-specific metric collection and anomaly detection. Our modular, containerized design enables reproducibility and provides a foundation for future enhancements, including dynamic slicing and AI-driven RAN optimization.

ABSTRACT: The Stochastic Job Shop Scheduling Problem (SJSSP) in a lineless mobile assembly system supported by Autonomous Mobile Robots (AMRs). ABSTRACT: Load balancing distributes incoming traffic across a pool of resources to improve system performance and prevent overutilization or underutilization of resources. The primary goal is to minimize task execution time while maximizing overall resource utilization in a heterogeneous environment, with a focus on optimizing memory and CPU usage. The proposed dynamic algorithm effectively adapts to handle numerous tasks and fluctuating nodes. Simulations are conducted using ‎CloudSim. The performance is compared with existing PSO variants: Time-Conscious PSO, PPTS-PSO, EASA-MORU, and ‎HEPGA. Results show that ‎the proposed method significantly outperforms other existing approaches. Specifically, the algorithm achieves an average resource utilization of 98%, reduces execution time, improves throughput, and ensures fair workload distribution across all nodes. The proposed method is highly suitable for distributed computing environments characterized by dynamic task demands and varying computational resource requirements.

ABSTRACT: This paper introduces YOLO-OptiMob, a comprehensive pipeline for optimizing YOLO11 models for deployment on edge devices. The process begins with creating and preprocessing a custom dataset featuring seven object classes: bike, car, cat, dog, person, handbag, and water bottle. The YOLO11 model is trained on this dataset and optimized using L1 unstructured pruning, with rates of 30%, 40%, and 50% evaluated. Based on the results, a 40% pruning rate was selected as it offered the best balance between model size reduction and accuracy retention. Post-training INT8 quantization further compresses the model, reducing its size from 11.4 to 2.5 MB. ABSTRACT: Adversarial attacks pose a significant challenge to the robustness of deep neural networks (DNNs), particularly in sensitive applications such as image classification. We propose a comprehensive approach to enhance the resilience of DNNs by integrating three advanced techniques: Robust Artificial Immune Learning System (RAILS), Jacobian regularization, and label smoothing. This combination of methods specifically addresses gaps in existing defenses by introducing an innovative multi-step process through RAILS, which works synergistically with Jacobian regularization and label smoothing to provide a balanced improvement in both adversarial robustness and model accuracy. Label smoothing reduces overconfidence in predictions, ensuring improved generalization, while Jacobian regularization reduces model sensitivity to input variations, thereby increasing robustness. RAILS, inspired by the immune system, introduces a multi-step process involving sensing, flocking, affinity maturation, and consensus, fostering adversarially robust learning in a way that existing approaches do not. Experimental results on the MNIST dataset demonstrate a 46.13% improvement in testing accuracy, from 52.80 to 98.93%, by increasing the number of hidden layers, with a decrease in adversarial accuracy from 96.66 to 88.59%. This trade-off between testing accuracy and adversarial robustness was effectively managed by incorporating regularization and augmentation techniques, ensuring that the model remains both highly accurate on clean data and resilient to adversarial attacks. Finally, we outline potential avenues for further research to extend these techniques to more complex datasets and real-world scenarios, particularly emphasizing the novelty of combining RAILS with established methods for adversarial defense, which provides a robust foundation for future advancements in DNN robustness

ABSTRACT: Humans communicate to share information and build relationships with each other. This method uses modalities such as speech, hand gestures, and facial expressions to communicate with others. Despite the prevalence of spoken communication, individuals with speech and hearing impairments heavily rely on nonverbal modes of communication such as hand gestures and facial expressions. Hearing-impaired individuals communicate through visual language which uses hand gestures, facial expression, and body movements to convey the information. Indian Sign Language (ISL) is other sign language rich in syntax, context, and grammar. Education systems, other public sectors should have flexibility to communicate with hearing-impaired individuals as well. Hence this work aims to build Sign Spotting method which helps in the accessibility of signs in the sign language data. This work presents the method for spotting Indian sign language at word levels in a continuous sign language video. For this task, publicly available ISL data was used, but customized it as per requirement by annotating gloss signs in multiple Indian sign language videos which have starting and ending timestamp. Our work helps to predict the gloss signs and their respective start and end timestamps in a continuous ISL video. This work uses Inflated-3D model and Spatial–Temporal models for extracting important features from the videos. Then use a temporal module for concatenating and spotting the signs. The precision, recall, and F1-score of our work are 0.545, 0.514, and 0.529, respectively. This is calculated using Intersection over Union (IoU) technique to get a better insight about the results. This methodology aims to enhance the accuracy and adaptability of sign language recognition systems, contributing to a more effective and inclusive approach in interpreting Indian Sign Language

ABSTRACT: The dramatic growth of mobile devices and the use of user data will result in exceptional difficulties to manage in the current mobile network. Next generation network 5G and Mobile Edge Computing (MEC) technologies are the desired solutions to manage the resources of mobile networks. Quality of Services (QoS) of end to end mobile network can be provided by combining MEC network with 5G. MEC is an intermediate network between end devices and back bone network. The end device network may include varity of Internet of Things (IoT) enabled 5G applications. MEC servers are processing huge amount data received from the users. This overburdens the MEC servers. Resources like Band Width (BW) management is necessary. So balancing the load of servers is essential for efficiency usage of BW. Service efficiency, system performance, and operating costs have been improved by using appropriate load balancing algorithm on MEC servers. The authors have introduced mobility load balancing in MEC network with 5G to prevent service interruptions due to unequal load. The proposed algorithm Load Balancing Efficiency Factor (LBEF) considers the load on MEC server connected to different neighbouring cells. Edge user equipment of each of the overloaded cells are considered to determine the load efficiency factor. It specifies the sequence of overloaded cells and starts offloading process in them. The proposed method of load balancing on MEC servers in 5G increases the throughput of network with minimal standard deviation

ABSTRACT: The utilization of Deep Neural Network (DNN) models is widespread in various commercial applications, including virtual assistants and chatbots, as well as across diverse domains such as manufacturing, medical, autonomous driving, defense, and security. While these models exhibit exceptional accuracy, their high computational, storage, and power requirements pose challenges for deployment on edge devices. To overcome these constraints, our previous work introduced a novel optimizer called “SparPen,” designed explicitly for filter pruning. It significantly surpasses the current state-of-the-art filter pruning technique called Stripe-Wise Pruning (SWP). ABSTRACT: Few-shot learning is essential for tasks involving limited labeled data, where traditional deep learning models often face challenges. This paper provides a comprehensive comparative analysis of four prominent few-shot learning techniques: Prototypical Networks, Siamese Networks, Relation Networks, and Matching Networks. These methods are evaluated using key performance metrics, including accuracy, inference time, and GFLOPS, to determine their suitability for various application scenarios. Our experimental results show that Prototypical Networks achieve the highest classification accuracy of 90.38%, making them ideal for applications such as medical image diagnosis and anomaly detection in industrial settings. Siamese Networks excel in inference speed and computational efficiency, making them well-suited for low-resource environments, such as facial recognition on mobile devices. While Relation Networks require higher computational resources, they offer competitive accuracy and can be utilized in e-commerce for personalized product recommendations. Matching Networks provide balanced performance, making them effective for dynamic environments like real-time inventory tracking in retail. However, challenges remain, including limited dataset diversity impacting generalization, scalability issues with computationally intensive methods, and difficulties in handling intra-class variability and noisy data. Future work will explore advanced optimization techniques, such as quantization and pruning, to further reduce computational overhead and improve deployment feasibility on edge devices. Additionally, efforts will focus on extending the application of these models to real-world challenges, including wildlife conservation through species identification and disaster response via rapid visual data analysis

ABSTRACT:

ABSTRACT: Colorectal cancer is one of the leading causes of cancer-related mortality worldwide, necessitating efficient and accurate diagnostic approaches. This study proposes a deep learning-based ensemble model for the detection and classification of colorectal cancer using histopathological images from the CRC-VAL-HE-7K dataset, comprising 7,190 images across nine classes. Four state-of-the-art convolutional neural networks (CNNs) were employed: ResNet-50, VGG-19, MobileNet V4, and Inception V4 for feature extraction and classification, with predictions aggregated using a majority voting strategy. Manual annotation of rib fractures in CT scans remains a labor-intensive and error-prone process, heavily reliant on the radiologist‘s expertise. ABSTRACT: Our paper presents a multimodal kannada-to-english translation system based on the mT5large transformer model, fine-tuned on the AI4Bharat Samanantar dataset. Designed to support three input modalities—typed kannada text, images containing printed kannada script, and spoken kannada audio—the system facilitates seamless translation across diverse formats using a unified architecture. For image inputs, Tesseract OCR with the kannada language pack is used to extract text from scanned documents or photographs. For audio, the system employs OpenAI’s Whisper model to transcribe kannada speech into text with high fidelity. The extracted or directly entered text is then processed by the fine-tuned mT5 model to generate english translations. Our approach effectively integrates state-of-the-art technologies in Optical Character Recognition (OCR), Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR), and neural machine translation, demonstrating their combined utility in addressing the linguistic challenges associated with low-resource languages. Evaluation of the system yields a BLEU score of 0.5583, a ChrF score of 67.4113, and a TER score of 26, indicating competitive translation quality. The high accuracy across multiple input types highlights the robustness of the system and its ability to generalize across various forms of user interaction. Our research contributes toward inclusive language technologies by enabling kannada speakers to access digital content and services in english, thus supporting broader applications in education, accessibility, and public service delivery. ABSTRACT: Physician shortages, rising patient numbers, and urgent clinical judgments are putting increasing strain on health-care systems around the world, especially in settings with limited resources and little access to advanced diagnostic assistance. Large Language Models (LLMs) automate medical documentation, assisting in patient triage, and supporting diagnostic workflows, yet their deployment remains impractical: a 70 billion parameter model requires 140 GB of memory in full precision, inference latency exceeds clinical acceptability on standard hardware, and privacy regulations crutial on-premise deployment that most facilities cannot support. This survey addresses the deployment gap by analyzing optimization techniques that make LLaMA models available for real-world medical applications. We evaluate three quantization methods (GPTQ, AWQ, NF4) that compress model weights to 4-bit precision, and three parameter-efficient fine-tuning approaches (LoRA, QLoRA, AdaLoRA) that enable domain adaptation by training only 0.01-0.1% of model parameters. Experimental evaluation on WikiText-2 and MMLU benchmarks demonstrates that quantization achieves 3.5-4× memory reduction with 94-99% accuracy retention across models from 7B to 65B parameters, while PEFT methods maintain 95-99% of full fine-tuning performance. Combined optimization enables a 70B model to operate within 48 GB memory with sub-2-second inference on consumer GPUs—practical for clinical deployment. Analysis of PMC-LLaMA shows that LoRA fine-tuning improved MedQA-USMLE accuracy from 36.1% to 56.4% using only 0.036% trainable parameters. While identifying important gaps in domain-specific quantization, regulatory validation frameworks, and uncertainty quantification that need more research, our findings demonstrate that the strategic integration of quantization and parameter-efficient fine-tuning increases access to advanced medical AI by allowing resource-constrained facilities to deploy models previously only available to well-funded research institutions

ABSTRACT: Ensuring factual reliability has become a key requirement in Education Technology (EdTech), especially as Large Language Models (LLMs) are being used more and more for better personalized learning and tutoring. On their own, LLMs often rely on static training data, which can make their responses outdated or sometimes inaccurate due to hallucinations. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) was designed to ground LLMs with external data sources, yet most traditional RAG setups that depend on plain text still struggle to provide sufficient context for complex and domain-specific problems. These gaps make it difficult to apply such systems in sensitive domains where accuracy is crucial. This survey studies an emerging approach called Knowledge Graph Enhanced RAG (KG-RAG). It reviews recent works that combine knowledge graphs with RAG models across multiple domains, such as biology, cybersecurity, and education, grouping them by their architectural patterns including hybrid retrieval and graph-based context expansion. The collected findings, such as a 35.2% improvement in student assessment results and an 18.7% accuracy increase in biomedical QA, show that KG-RAG methods consistently outperform standard RAG models. The purpose of this review is to consolidate these developments and highlight open challenges to support the creation of more dependable and domain-aware AI systems

ABSTRACT: With the growing reliance on electronic devices, the generation of electronic waste (e-waste) has surged, presenting significant environmental and health hazards when improperly handled. Traditional methods of sorting and classifying e-waste typically relies on manual processes that are time-consuming and prone to errors. Our paper proposes a quantized YOLOv12-based automated system for detecting e-waste. The training process utilized a tailored dataset comprising 23 typical e-waste categories, such as laptops, smartphones, irons, microwaves, and washing machines. Evaluation on the test dataset showed that the model attained a mean Average Precision of 0.953 at mAP@0.5 and 0.718 at mAP@0.5:0.95, with a precision of 0.847 and recall of 0.576 across all classes. Notably, classes like light bulb achieved high precision (1.0) but low recall, while classes like washing machine showed full recall (1.0) and strong overall performance. The trained YOLOv12 model was quantized and converted into TensorFlow Lite format and deployed in an Android application. The app performs real-time e-waste detection using the device’s live camera feed, drawing bounding boxes and labels on detected objects. This lightweight, on-device solution can support individuals, recyclers, and local authorities in identifying and managing e-waste efficiently, promoting responsible disposal and environmental sustainability
